title: Redwood Migration Demo: OpenAI+Anthropic->Redwood (parity)
summary: Demo focused on mapping OpenAI/Anthropic/Together API features to Redwood equivalents, discussing parity for generation, streaming, function calling, embeddings, and security requirements. Agreed next steps: share parity mapping doc, run perf benchmarks, start a 2-week pilot on Dedicated or Hosted with sample traffic.
topics: Dedicated vs Hosted vs Private deployment

header: Date: 2026-03-20 | Time: 16:00 PDT | Duration: 52 minutes | Attendees: Alex Morgan (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Michael Lee (Acadia), Sara Gomez (Acadia), Tom Nguyen (Acadia)
transcript:
[00:00] Alex: Hi everybody, thanks for joining, I'm Alex Morgan from Redwood, AE on this account, with Priya Shah our SE. I'll hand it to Priya to do the product walkthrough and we'll pause for questions.
[00:15] Priya: Hey team, thanks. Quick agenda, we'll cover API parity mapping from OpenAI/Anthropic/Together to Redwood, the Console/Optimize features, and then security/compliance notes and next steps. We'll show live examples for generation, streaming, function calling and embeddings.
[00:38] Michael: Sounds good. Our core ask is simple — we want to migrate with minimal client changes and keep output parity, and we care about latency and TCO.
[00:50] Priya: Totally. First, high level, Redwood API is REST/SDK compatible; we map common endpoints. For text generation the param names are similar but note: model naming differs, default temperature and top_p behavior may vary slightly — we'll provide mapping.
[01:10] Sara: Is there a tokenization difference? We use tiktoken now with OpenAI.
[01:18] Priya: Good question. Redwood supports the same tokenization families; for most OpenAI models tiktoken mapping is 1:1. For some open models tokenization differs and that affects prompt length — we call that out in the parity doc.
[01:32] Alex: Quick note — we prefer to test on a few canonical prompts to validate exact parity, we'll share a harness.
[01:40] Tom: On streaming and function calling — Anthropic and Together have different function schemas, how does Redwood handle that?
[01:50] Priya: Redwood has streaming responses and a function-calling abstraction. Implementation wise our 'tool call' payload maps to OpenAI-style function calls, and we can accept Anthropic-style structured outputs via a compatibility layer. In practice we'll show curl examples.
[02:12] Priya: (shares link) Deck: https://redwood.ai/deck/migration-parity — contains detailed param mappings and recommended temp/top_p defaults. Benchmark sheet: https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-benchmarks - sample throughput numbers.
[02:35] Michael: Nice, we'll look. On embeddings — we use 1536-d embeddings from OpenAI currently; Together has 1024 dims sometimes — can Redwood host mixed dims?
[02:48] Priya: Yes, Redwood supports multiple embedding families. We recommend reindexing if your vector store expects a single dimension. For some customers we provide on-the-fly conversion or indicate model mapping to keep parity.
[03:05] Sara: Any differences in cost units? We bill tokens+embedding units?
[03:10] Alex: Hosted is usage-based per-token/per-embedding, similar math. Dedicated is capacity-based which may be better for steady high throughput. We'll show cost modeling in the spreadsheet.
[03:23] Tom: Latency — can we get comparable p95 to what we have now with OpenAI?
[03:30] Priya: For short prompts and standard seq lengths, hosted p95 is similar; Dedicated can be tuned for lower tail latency. We also offer KV cache and prefix caching that reduces repeated-context token compute. Note: if you go quantized model variants you get lower cost but slightly higher latency in some cases.
[03:55] Michael: You mentioned KV cash — did you mean KV cache? (laugh)
[04:00] Priya: Sorry, yes KV cache, transcription humor.
[04:05] Alex: Security — SOC2, SSO/SAML, KMS support?
[04:10] Priya: Yes. Hosted is SOC2 compliant; we offer enterprise agreements for private deployments with customer-managed KMS/HSM integrations. SAML SSO and RBAC are supported in console. We'll share our security pack.
[04:27] Michael: We need audit logs and per-route observability for compliance.
[04:32] Priya: Console exposes token-level cost and latency breakdowns, per-route dashboards, and audit logs for inference requests.
[04:42] Sara: Any gotchas when migrating prompt engineering? We've seen differences in output formatting.
[04:49] Priya: Minor adjustments sometimes required; that's why we recommend a canary and a prompt regression suite — Redwood Optimize supports evals tied to prompt sets so you can get alerts on regressions.
[05:05] Tom: For the POC, we want to test both hosted and Dedicated to see cost/latency tradeoffs. Does Redwood let us fall back between them?
[05:15] Alex: Yes, Smart Routing can direct traffic by policy and fall back to hosted variants if Dedicated capacity is saturated.
[05:25] Priya: Let's demo a live generation. I'll run an OpenAI prompt we received earlier and show Redwood's equivalent. (typing)
[06:05] Priya: Streaming example: curl --location 'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate' -d '{"model":"redwood-v1","prompt":"Write a product blurb about...","stream":true}' and you get chunked events. For function calls: we accept a functions array similar to OpenAI where you define name/parameters, Redwood will return a structured tool call event.
[06:40] Michael: Are the event formats identical? We have parsers expecting specific JSON shapes.
[06:46] Priya: We try to be compatible; small differences exist in the envelope. We'll give exact curl+parsers.
[06:55] Sara: What about rate limits and quotas? We have bursty traffic during releases.
[07:00] Alex: Hosted has rate limits and quotas configurable per account; Dedicated gives you reserved QPS and autoscaling policies with burst capacity. We'll share recommended autoscale configs.
[07:15] Tom: Private deployment — can we run Redwood in our VPC?
[07:20] Priya: Yes, Private includes a customer-managed control plane and on-prem package if you need air-gapped. We can support KMS in VPC and audit log forwarding.
[07:32] Michael: Great. Let's talk data retention and logs for PII — we need logs purged after 90 days and redact PII.
[07:40] Priya: We support configurable retention and data redaction pipelines; for private deployments customers can ensure retention via their infra.
[07:48] Alex: For migration checklist — key items: mapping models, tokenization, embedding dims, function call schema, rate-limit & retry logic, prompt regression tests, benchmark runs. We'll send that doc.
[08:05] Priya: On benchmarks — we typically run a 3-phase test: dry-run with synthetic traffic, realistic traffic replay, and tail-latency stress. Our benchmark sheet includes test scripts and sample results.
[08:20] Michael: Ok, what about Together/TogetherAI specifics? They do model sharding and different batch sizes.
[08:28] Priya: For Together models we map to comparable Redwood-verified variants and pick quantization profiles; batch behavior can be adjusted by kernel selection. We'll outline recommended batch sizes per model in the sheet.
[08:45] Sara: Any SDK changes? We call openai.ChatCompletion and have webhook parsers.
[08:52] Priya: Redwood SDKs have helper functions mirroring chat APIs; for webhooks we can emit the same webhook event shapes or provide a lightweight adapter. We'll include snippets.
[09:05] Tom: If we need on-call support during POC, is that available?
[09:10] Alex: Yes SE-supported POCs include a runbook and escalation path. For Dedicated/Private we offer a higher SLA with option for 24/7 support.
[09:20] Michael: Pricing — do you have a simple estimate for 5M tokens/month + 50k embeddings?
[09:28] Alex: We'll model that in the spreadsheet and include both hosted per-token and Dedicated commit options. Expect similar to slightly lower TCO depending on cache hit rate and batching.
[09:42] Priya: Quick demo of Console Optimize — shows batching recommendations, quantization suggestions, and cost impact simulation. (shares screen) You can upload a prompt set and it will simulate cost delta vs different models.
[10:10] Sara: That looks useful. For the POC we'll probably start with hosted for speed then evaluate Dedicated after 1 week.
[10:20] Alex: Sounds reasonable. Let's capture next steps.
[10:25] Tom: A couple security items — we need pen-test report and your SOC2 scope doc.
[10:30] Priya: We'll attach SOC2 report and pen-test summary in the security pack link.
[10:36] Alex: Ok wrapping up — agreed actions are in the next steps. We'll send parity doc, bench templates, and sample curl/SDK snippets.
[10:50] Michael: Thanks everyone, good walkthrough. We'll review and get Sara to send logs.
[10:56] Sara: Thanks, bye.
[11:00] Alex: Bye all, we'll follow up via email with links and propose POC dates.
[11:05] End of call. Note: transcription contains minor mis-hears (e.g., KV cash).
